tasks.title: Effective value in sshd_config
tasks.statement: Write a function sshd_value(config, key, user, groups, addr): the value of the setting key for an incoming connection of user (a string) who belongs to groups (a list of strings) and comes from addr (a string). config is the text of sshd_config. Rules. Blank lines and lines that start with # (after spaces) are skipped. The setting word and the criterion word are case-insensitive, arguments are case-sensitive. The value is the rest of the line with runs of spaces collapsed to one. For most settings the first value found is used and the rest are ignored. The exception is the accumulating settings allowusers, denyusers, allowgroups, denygroups, port and listenaddress: the values of all applicable lines are taken, joined with one space. Lines before the first Match apply to every connection. A Match line opens a block that lasts until the next Match; its arguments are either the single word All (matches everyone) or pairs 'criterion patterns' with the criteria user, group and address; the block applies when all criteria are satisfied. Patterns are a comma-separated list; * and ? are wildcards; a leading ! negates a pattern: if any negated pattern matches, the criterion fails, otherwise at least one positive pattern must match. user is compared with user, group with any of groups, address with addr; an address pattern that contains / is a CIDR network (the address must lie inside it), all others are plain wildcards. A Match with an unknown criterion never applies. Lines outside an applying block are skipped. If the setting is absent, return an empty string.
tasks.hint: Keep an active flag (True before the first Match) and recompute it on each Match line. For an ordinary setting return at the first applicable line, for accumulating ones collect a list.

tasks.title: The client ssh_config
tasks.statement: Write a function ssh_effective(config, host): the resulting ssh client settings for the command 'ssh host'. Return a dictionary whose keys are the setting names in lower case and whose values are strings. config is the text of ~/.ssh/config. A setting line is a word and a value separated by spaces or by an = sign (spaces around = are allowed); the value is the rest of the line trimmed at both ends. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Lines before the first Host line apply to every host. A Host line holds one or more patterns separated by spaces (* and ? are wildcards, case matters); the block lasts until the next Host line and applies if host matches at least one positive pattern and no pattern with a leading ! (a pattern with ! alone includes nothing). Patterns are compared with host exactly as typed in the command; the hostname setting does not affect matching. For each setting the first value found is used. The exception is identityfile: in the result it is a list of strings that collects all values from all applying blocks in order of appearance. config contains no Match lines.
tasks.hint: Split a line with the regular expression (\S+?)(?:\s*=\s*|\s+)(.*). For Host: if a negated pattern matches, the block does not apply; otherwise a positive match is needed.

tasks.title: Parsing authorized_keys
tasks.statement: Write a function parse_authorized_keys(text): parse an authorized_keys file and return a list of tuples (options, keytype, comment) in line order. A line is: optional options, the key type, the key in base64, an optional comment (the rest of the line trimmed at both ends, otherwise an empty string). Blank lines and lines starting with # (after spaces) are skipped. Known types: ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com, sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com. If the first word of the line is a key type, there are no options. Otherwise the first word is the options: it may contain spaces only inside double quotes, and inside quotes \" is a quote character. Lines in which no known type and key (at least one word after the type) follow the options are skipped. Options is a comma-separated list (a comma inside quotes does not separate); an item is name or name=value. The options in the result form a dictionary: names in lower case; True for a name without a value; for name=value the value string with the surrounding quotes removed and \" replaced by ". If a name repeats, the first occurrence is kept. Without options return an empty dictionary.
tasks.hint: First find the end of the first word, taking quotes and backslashes into account; then split the options on commas outside quotes with a separate helper.

tasks.title: What an authorized_keys line allows
tasks.statement: Write a function key_access(opts, addr, now, request): the decision for a key login. opts is the options dictionary of one authorized_keys line (as from parsing: lower-case names, True for flags, strings for values), addr is the client address, now is the current time as the string YYYYMMDDHHMMSS (UTC), request is one of: "shell", "exec:<command>", "pty", "port-forward", "agent-forward", "x11-forward". The checks run in order. 1) If from is present: it is a comma-separated pattern list; a pattern with a leading ! is a negation; a pattern with / is a CIDR network, otherwise * and ? are wildcards over the text of the address. The address is allowed if at least one positive pattern matches and no negated one does; otherwise return "denied:from". 2) If expiry-time is present (YYYYMMDD or YYYYMMDDHHMM or YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, possibly with a trailing Z that is ignored): pad the value on the right with zeros to 14 digits; if now is not less than it, return "denied:expired". 3) For "shell" and "exec:...": if command is present return "run:" followed by the value of command (the client's command is replaced), otherwise "ok". 4) For the other requests the capability is named pty, port-forwarding, agent-forwarding, x11-forwarding respectively. The capability is off if the flag no-<name> is present; otherwise on if the flag <name> is present; otherwise off if restrict is present; otherwise on. Return an off capability as "denied:" plus the capability name, an on one as "ok".
tasks.hint: now and the expiry can be compared as strings of equal length. For capabilities write a small function cap(name) with three checks in order.

tasks.title: Checking a host key against known_hosts
tasks.statement: Write a function known_hosts_check(text, host, port, key_type, key_blob): what the ssh client answers to a presented host key. text is the content of known_hosts, host is the name, port is the port number (an int), key_type and key_blob are the key type and its base64. The name to look up is host for port 22 and '[host]:port' for any other port, in lower case. A file line is: an optional marker (@cert-authority or @revoked), the hosts field, the key type, the base64 (the rest is a comment). Blank lines, lines starting with # and lines with fewer than three fields are skipped; lines with @cert-authority and with any other marker are ignored. The hosts field matches as follows: if it starts with |, it is a hashed name '|1|salt|hash' (salt and hash in base64): take the HMAC-SHA1 of the looked-up name keyed with the decoded salt and compare its base64 with the hash; otherwise it is a comma-separated pattern list (* and ? are wildcards, case-insensitive) where a leading ! negates: a matching negated pattern makes the line not match, otherwise at least one positive pattern must match. A key equals the presented one if both the type and the base64 are equal. The answer is a string: "revoked" if a host-matching @revoked line holds the presented key (regardless of line order); else "ok" if a host-matching ordinary line holds this key; else "changed" if at least one host-matching ordinary line holds a different key (even of another type); else "unknown".
tasks.hint: First decide whether the line matches the host, then compare the key. The hash is base64(hmac.new(b64decode(salt), name.encode(), sha1).digest()).

tasks.title: A sudo decision from sudoers
tasks.statement: Write a function sudo_decision(sudoers, user, groups, command): what sudo tells user (a member of groups) who asks to run command (a string such as "/usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx"). Return "deny", "password" or "nopasswd". A simplified model of sudoers. A line that ends in \ is joined with the next one (a space replaces the \). Blank lines, lines starting with #, Defaults and @include/@includedir are skipped. User_Alias name = list and Cmnd_Alias name = list define aliases; a list is comma-separated items; aliases are defined above their uses and do not nest, except that a User_Alias may hold names, %groups and ALL. Every other line is a rule: 'users ALL = [(runas)] commands'. Users is a comma-separated list: ALL, a name, a %group or an alias (no negation); the word ALL before = is the host field and is ignored. The optional (runas) right after = is ignored. Commands is a comma-separated list; an item may be preceded by the tags NOPASSWD: or PASSWD: (a tag applies to that item and all following items of the rule until another tag; every rule starts with PASSWD). An item is ALL, a command path, a path with arguments or a Cmnd_Alias name; an item may be preceded by ! (a negation, applied to the whole alias). A path without arguments matches any arguments, a path with arguments matches only exactly that command (whitespace is normalised), ALL matches any command. Rules and items are scanned in order and the last matching item wins: a negated one gives "deny", an ordinary one gives "nopasswd" when NOPASSWD is in force and "password" otherwise. If nothing matched, "deny".
tasks.hint: Join the lines, build the alias dictionaries, then walk the rules: if the user matches, go through the items and remember the result of the last matching one.

tasks.title: A public key fingerprint
tasks.statement: Write a function key_fingerprint(pubkey_line, algo): the fingerprint as 'ssh-keygen -l' prints it. pubkey_line is a public key line 'type base64 [comment]'; algo is "sha256" or "md5". Decode the base64 into the bytes blob. Inside blob the first field is 4 bytes of length (big-endian) followed by a string of that length: it is the key type and must equal the type in pubkey_line. For sha256 return 'SHA256:' and the base64 of the SHA-256 of the whole blob without trailing = characters. For md5 return 'MD5:' and the 16 bytes of the MD5 of the blob as 32 lower-case hex digits split into pairs with colons. If the line has fewer than two words, the base64 is invalid, the blob is shorter than it declares, the types differ, or algo is anything else, return an empty string.
tasks.hint: Use base64 (b64decode with validate=True) and hashlib; read the type length with int.from_bytes(blob[:4], 'big').

tasks.title: A ProxyJump chain
tasks.statement: Write a function jump_chain(config, target, default_user): the list of hops ssh goes through to reach target. config is a dictionary 'Host alias → dictionary of settings' whose possible keys are hostname (a string), user (a string), port (an int) and proxyjump (a string). target is what is typed in the ssh command; default_user is the user name if neither the command nor config gives one. A hop is the string 'user@hostname:port'. Parsing a name (for the target and for a jump): an optional 'user@' at the start, an optional ':port' at the end, the rest is the alias; if the alias is not in config, it serves as the host name itself and has no settings. The values come from: user - the name, else the settings, else default_user; hostname - the settings, else the alias itself; port - the name, else the settings, else 22. The proxyjump setting is a comma-separated list of jumps (none means no jumps); they are walked in order, and each jump's own proxyjump from config applies too (its chain first, then the jump itself). The result lists the hops of the jumps in connection order, with the target itself last. If the chain ever comes back to an alias that is already being expanded higher up the chain (a loop), return an empty list.
tasks.hint: A recursive function expand(spec, seen): parse spec, call expand with seen | {alias} for each jump in proxyjump, then append the own hop.

tasks.title: Detached tmux sessions
tasks.statement: Write a function detached_sessions(ls_output): parse the output of 'tmux ls' and return a list of tuples (name, window_count) for the sessions nobody is attached to right now, from the newest to the oldest by creation time; on a tie by name ascending. An output line looks like 'name: N windows (created Tue Nov  3 11:37:04 2026)', optionally followed by ' (group group_name)' and ' (attached)', in that order, each part optional. The name may contain spaces but no colon. The word 'windows' is spelled so even for one window. The date is a weekday, a month (Jan...Dec, three letters), the day (a single-digit day may have an extra space before it), the time HH:MM:SS and the year. A session is attached if the line has ' (attached)'. Lines that do not look like a session description (for example 'no server running on /tmp/tmux-1000/default') are skipped.
tasks.hint: One regular expression with optional groups; turn the date into a tuple (year, month number, day, hour, minute, second) and sort in two passes: by name, then by time descending (the sort is stable).

tasks.title: Will sshd let the user in
tasks.statement: Write a function login_possible(settings, user, method, forced): can user log in with method ("key" or "password"). settings is a dictionary of effective sshd settings (lower-case names, string values; a missing setting means the default). forced is a bool: whether the user's key has a command option. The checks run in order. 1) denyusers: a space-separated pattern list (* and ? are wildcards); if user matches at least one - False. 2) allowusers: if the list is non-empty and user matches none of the patterns - False. 3) For user == "root", permitrootlogin applies (default prohibit-password): no - False; prohibit-password and its synonym without-password - False for password; forced-commands-only - False for password, and for key False when forced is False; yes forbids nothing. 4) For method "key", pubkeyauthentication (default yes) must be yes; for "password", passwordauthentication (default yes) must be yes; values are compared case-insensitively. Any other method - False.
tasks.hint: First the two user lists, then the root branch, then whether the method itself is enabled.
